root_cause_class: Open_Redirect (CWE-601) via X-Forwarded-Prefix — NOT path traversal
note_on_scaffold: The CASE_INDEX scaffold labelled this pair Path_Traversal/read-exfil. Reading the official advisories and the fix commit shows both CVEs are open-redirect (protocol-relative Location) via X-Forwarded-Prefix. Labels corrected to Open_Redirect / redirect-canary.
incomplete_fix_quote: It was found that the fix for CVE-2026-27738 was incomplete: the validation blocked prefixes starting with multiple leading slashes (e.g. '///') but failed to account for a single leading backslash ('\'). The application prepends a leading forward slash, resulting in a '/\' sequence in the Location header, which browsers treat as '//' (a protocol-relative URL) and follow to an attacker-controlled domain (CVE-2026-33397).
root_cause: packages/angular/ssr/src/utils/{url.ts,validation.ts}: the 27738 fix (commit f086ecc) made joinUrlParts strip all leading slashes and added INVALID_PREFIX_REGEX=/^[/\\]{2}|(?:^|[/\\])\.\.?(?:[/\\]|$)/. That regex requires TWO leading slash/backslash chars, so a single leading backslash slips through; joinUrlParts strips only forward-slashes, so '\<host>' -> Location '/\<host>/...' (protocol-relative). 20.3.21 (PR #32771) hardens the regex to /^(?:\\|\/[/\\])|.../ which also rejects a single leading backslash.
